q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
Short answer: your premise is reversed in the data — ROAS fell while net profit improved. Measured evidence below; see hypotheses and next steps to diagnose drivers.

Measured (period = 2026-09-13 → 2026-10-12 vs previous 2026-08-14 → 2026-09-12)
- Net profit (P&L, order_date) — previous: -₹5,69,638 → current: -₹40,679. Measured (from order_pnl; freshed 2026-10-13T18:08Z).  
- Product P&L net ROAS (allocated) — previous: 0.5889 → current: -0.2513. Measured (product_pnl; freshed 2026-10-13T18:08Z).

What that means (tags)
- Measured: Net profit moved from a larger loss to a much smaller loss (improved). Product P&L net ROAS moved from ~0.59 to -0.25 (worse).  
- Hypothesis: the apparent “ROAS up / profit down” story cannot be true for these metrics and this period — instead ROAS worsened while profit improved. Possible explanations (not yet tested): (1) you were looking at a different ROAS definition (e.g., gross ROAS, platform ROAS or product vs company ROAS) — different ROAS definitions can move opposite to P&L ROAS; (2) timing/attribution differences between product-level allocated ROAS and company net profit (P&L) — allocation or unallocated costs can change profit independently; (3) lower ad spend concentrated on high-margin SKUs or lower refunds/discounts reduced losses even as some ROAS ratio fell; (4) data-scope mismatch (product_pnl_net_roas vs a platform-reported ROAS).
